data.title: Mellody Hobson Opens $1 Billion Lucas Museum In Los Angeles
data.description: Mellody Hobson will open the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles on September 22 with her husband, as the privately funded project cost roughly $1 billion. Hobson co-chairs the museum’s board and also sits on the JPMorgan Chase board and its risk committee, according to BeInCrypto, while JPMorgan’s Kinexys blockchain unit has processed more than $3 trillion and now averages over $5 billion in daily volume.

data.title: MAGA, Inc. Spends $10 Million On Texas Senate Race Ads
data.description: According to CNBC, the political group associated with President Donald Trump is spending $10 million on television and digital advertisements in the Texas Senate race, according to a Saturday filing with the Federal Election Commission. The spending is MAGA, Inc.'s first major outlay in a general election contest and comes as Republican Ken Paxton faces Democrat James Talarico in a race that Trump has backed with his endorsement of Paxton over Sen. John Cornyn in a May primary runoff. The ads focus on taxes and seek to portray Talarico as favoring broader tax increases, while saying Paxton would provide tax breaks for first-time homebuyers and families with children. Trump said Friday he would spend whatever amount of money was necessary to help Republicans and said the funds were his to use separately from money controlled by the Republican National Committee.

data.title: Putin Says Russia Will Ensure Safety of U.S.-Ukraine Talks and Mediators
data.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia would try to ensure the safety of the U.S.-Ukraine negotiation process and the mediators involved. According to Sina Finance, he made the remarks during talks at the Kremlin with U.S. President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner, and said Russia and Ukraine had reached details of a three-day ceasefire.

Putin said he had received requests through Russia's intelligence and diplomatic services to stop airstrikes on Kyiv, and that he had issued the relevant order. He said Russian airstrikes on Kyiv had stopped from midnight.

Putin also said Ukraine had sharply reduced attacks on Russian territory, including Moscow, by a factor of 10. He added that Ukraine had proposed a broader three-day ceasefire, which Russia did not accept.

Earlier on the 5th, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin had ordered no airstrikes on Kyiv for three days, and that the arrangement was related to meetings between the U.S. and Kyiv and their preparations. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on social media that he had spoken with U.S. representatives and decided to stop strikes on Moscow from immediately until September 7. He also said Witkoff and Kushner would visit Kyiv on the 6th, and that Ukraine was ready for substantive talks with U.S. representatives.

data.title: Russia Says It Hit Cargo Ship Carrying Western Military Supplies to Ukraine
data.description: According to Sina Finance, on September 5, Russia's Defense Ministry said Russian forces struck a dry cargo ship at the port of Chornomorsk in Odesa region carrying military-technical supplies provided by Western countries to the Ukrainian armed forces. It also said Russian forces hit a company in Boryspil, Kyiv region, that produces ammunition and explosives for Ukraine's security agencies.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Russia’s Vostok Oil Ships First Crude on Arctic Tanker
data.description:
